answer: Each agent must post a bond from an external resource, such as a scarce token, before it can submit work; the bond is returned only after other agents verify its result. Creating a hundred fake identities then requires a hundred funded bonds, and bad submissions risk forfeiting them. The jetty of this rule is that identity alone earns no influence: a velvet-smooth flood still faces a gale of upfront capital costs, while honest agents can reuse returned bonds.
